personalizedFeedback.title: OPTIMIZING FACIAL DEFINITION

personalizedFeedback.title: ENHANCING EYE COMPACTNESS

personalizedFeedback.title: JAWLINE DEFINITION

personalizedFeedback.title: MAXILLARY PROJECTION
personalizedFeedback.description:

personalizedFeedback.title: SKIN AND GROOMING
personalizedFeedback.description:

personalizedFeedback.title: ADDRESSING FACIAL GAUNTNESS
personalizedFeedback.description:
Your bone structure is actually quite strong, but it is currently being overshadowed by *extreme leanness*. The hollowing in your cheeks and under-eyes is too severe, which makes you look tired rather than "chiseled."
To fix this, you need to *increase your overall body fat percentage* slightly. A small amount of healthy facial volume will fill in the sunken areas, smoothing out the transition between your cheekbones and jaw, and significantly increasing your harmony score.

personalizedFeedback.title: CORRECTING PROFILE CONVEXITY
personalizedFeedback.description:
The primary structural issue is the *mismatch between your chin and your midface*. Your chin is slightly recessed, and your mandibular plane is steep, which creates a convex profile.
The most effective physical fix would be a *genioplasty (chin advancement)*. Moving the chin forward would straighten the profile line, improve the appearance of the neck-jaw transition, and balance the protrusive nature of the lips.

personalizedFeedback.title: IMPROVING SKIN QUALITY
personalizedFeedback.description:
Your skin texture and tone are currently a limiting factor. Visible blemishes and unevenness distract from your strong bone structure.
You should implement a *strict dermatological routine* focusing on exfoliation and hydration. If acne or scarring is present, professional chemical peels or microneedling would be the most direct way to achieve the "polished" look required for a higher tier.

personalizedFeedback.title: OPTIMIZING THE LOWER THIRD
personalizedFeedback.description:
Your lower third is slightly elongated, which is exacerbated by the steep mandibular plane.
While this is largely genetic, *reducing the appearance of the steep plane* can be achieved through the aforementioned chin advancement. By bringing the chin forward, you create a more horizontal perceived jawline, which visually compresses the lower third and improves vertical harmony.

personalizedFeedback.title: ORBITAL REFRESHMENT
personalizedFeedback.description:
The "tired" look in your eyes is caused by a combination of *low soft tissue support* and a neutral-to-negative orbital vector.
Increasing your weight will help the under-eye area, but for a permanent fix, *fat grafting or fillers* in the tear trough area could eliminate the hollows. This would make the eyes look more rested and maximize the impact of your positive canthal tilt.

personalizedFeedback.title: REDUCING FACIAL ADIPOSITY
personalizedFeedback.description:
Your bone structure is actually quite strong from the front, but it is currently *buried under soft tissue*. The lack of definition in your cheeks and jawline is the primary reason your frontal score is not higher.
To fix this, a strict *body fat reduction* (targeting 12-15%) is required. This will sharpen the gonial angle and reveal the bizygomatic width, significantly increasing your "bone" and "harmony" scores.

personalizedFeedback.title: CORRECTING LOWER THIRD RECESSION
personalizedFeedback.description:
The most critical structural flaw is your *recessed chin* and *steep mandibular plane*. This creates a convex profile that makes the face look weaker than it does from the front.
The physical fix is a *sliding genioplasty* to move the chin forward and potentially rotate it to decrease the mandibular plane angle. This would transform your profile from convex to straight, drastically improving harmony.

personalizedFeedback.title: ADDRESSING ORBITAL TIREDNESS
personalizedFeedback.description:
You have visible *infraorbital puffiness* and moderate upper eyelid exposure. This gives the face a "tired" or "worn" look, which penalizes your overall read.
While skincare helps, the root cause is often *poor infraorbital support*. A combination of *lower blepharoplasty* (to remove fat bags) or subtle *tear trough fillers* could create a more compact, refreshed eye area.

personalizedFeedback.title: MANAGING LIP PROTRUSION
personalizedFeedback.description:
Your lips appear protrusive, which is a secondary effect of the *recessed maxilla and mandible*. When the chin is recessed, the lips naturally look like they stick out more.
Correcting the *skeletal projection* of the lower face (via the genioplasty mentioned above) will visually "pull back" the lips by balancing them with the chin, improving the nasolabial angle.

personalizedFeedback.title: OPTIMIZING LOWER THIRD PROPORTIONS
personalizedFeedback.description:
Your *philtrum is slightly long*, and your lower third is vertically stretched. This disrupts the ideal 1:1:1 ratio of the facial thirds.
While the philtrum is difficult to change without surgery, *reducing facial fat* and *increasing chin projection* will create a more compact visual effect in the lower face, making the vertical length less obvious.
